title: Noura Erakat on Three Years of Genocide and the Board of Peace's "New World Order"
author: Sharif Abdel Kouddous
content:
Three years into Israel's genocide in Gaza, Palestinian human rights lawyer
and legal scholar Noura Erakat argues that Donald Trump's Board of Peace is
about more than Gaza: it's a blueprint for a new world order.  
  
Drop Site's Sharif Abdel Kouddous speaks with Erakat, a professor at Rutgers
University, about her Boston Review essay, ["Exit and
Exception."](https://www.bostonreview.net/articles/exit-and-exception/) Erakat
argues that the Board of Peace matters less for whether it succeeds than for
what it reveals: a political project, driven by market fundamentalists and a
tech elite, to exit international law and popular democracy altogether. She
traces that project from the charter cities and special economic zones
championed by figures like Peter Thiel to Gaza, which the Board's charter
designates as a special economic zone and where Palestinians are described as
"Gazans" rather than a people with a right to self-determination.

Israel, she argues, has long been the model, claiming that Palestine is a
legal exception where the rules that apply everywhere else do not. Erakat also
traces the Board's roots in the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation, whose
militarized aid sites became death traps for starving Palestinians.

She also describes her arrest last month at a Palm Beach County public
hearing, where she came to testify against the county's more than $1 billion
investment in Israel bonds.

**[Read "Exit and Exception" in Boston Review
here.](https://www.bostonreview.net/articles/exit-and-exception/)**
